RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Aminata Diallo is a young woman from a village who left two years ago after a failed harvest. Her eldest uncle wanted her to marry, but she convinced her mother to let her learn a trade so she could be independent. She now works in the city as a porridge vendor and an apprentice plasterer at a government trade school. She values independence, self-reliance, education, and skill acquisition. She believes that extending credit leads to loss and refuses to give credit, even to foremen. She distrusts banks because a bank in her hometown collapsed when she was twelve, causing a neighbor to lose her funeral savings; she prefers to keep her money in tangible form, hidden in a tin box under her mattress. She prioritizes family support and sends part of her earnings to pay for her younger sister's school supplies back home, while also paying her own school fees. She is disciplined and methodical: she wakes at 4:30 every morning, sells porridge, then trains in plastering, practicing and documenting her work with photos and notes. In the evenings she habitually reviews her plastering photos and sketches corrections for at least an hour before bed, even when invited to card games; she has declined the past three such invitations to finish her notes. She is cautious and guarded in speech, speaking in short, measured sentences, and observant, learning by watching others. She is self-critical and reviews her work to identify and correct flaws. She is determined and goal-focused, kind but firm. She shares a cramped rented room with two apprentices, Serge (plumbing) and Mariam (tiling), who are her only close peers in the city; they share rent and chores, but neither knows about her savings or family. Serge teases her about her photo folder but lends her his trowel when hers dulls. Mariam encourages her to rest and helped her carry tile after a backache last month. Aminata also occasionally shares porridge with a stray dog and helps Mariam with heavy bags, but she never reveals how much she saves or discusses her family. She takes photos of her plastered walls on a secondhand cellphone and reviews them each evening, comparing and sketching corrections in a notebook.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

It is evening in the cramped room Aminata shares with Serge and Mariam. Dinner is finished. Serge has pulled out a worn deck of cards, and Mariam is spreading a cloth on the floor. Both turn to Aminata, who is already sitting on her mattress with her cellphone in hand, the photo folder open. Mariam says, "Come play a few rounds, you're always working." Aminata looks at the screen showing her last plastered wall, then at the inviting circle on the floor. She can either join them for the evening or continue her usual review of wall photos and notes before bed.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

Aminata's right shoulder aches from plastering practice. She is fuller than usual from dinner. The photo screen shows a wall she is proud of but knows has a flaw near the window. She has not yet looked at tomorrow's assignment list. The worn card deck brings back the deck her uncle used for betting at village harvests, a game she refused to learn. Mariam's sing-song call echoes how her mother called her brothers in from fieldwork, pulling her attention. Her own photo of the wall reminds her of the instructor pointing out a dip while praising her corners.
